blockers.summary: Regression mentioned: "…two commits in one to not introduce a regression by doing them separately. There were small changes required to unit tes…" (hudson-openstack)

The upstream backports stop at stable/2024.1. Ubuntu series or Cloud Archive pockets that ship older Neutron (for example Jammy/Yoga) have no available fix, so the target series for this SRU is unclear.

The fix only takes effect when `ovn.ovn_emit_need_to_frag` is set, and it needs an OVN version that supports it. The behaviour change is not default-on, and the required OVN version is not documented here, so verification and the regression-potential assessment need that stated.

The original fix introduced a regression (bug 2105383, wrong network_ids filter affecting redirect-type). The stable backports bundle the revert into one squashed change with conflict resolutions and modified unit tests. The Ubuntu SRU must carry both changes together, and the regression risk needs to be assessed.

Comment 25 proposed a maintenance task to update existing routers and networks. The merged change does not clearly include one, so existing deployments may not get gateway_mtu set after upgrade. This affects the test plan and the upgrade impact.

blockers.summary: The reviewer (juliank) says the problem has not been reproduced and understood from the boot side, so it is not yet clear the patch is correct. He wants this done before the patch is accepted.

The regression potential in the SRU template is wrong. os-prober is enabled automatically when other OSes are detected at install time, so more users are affected than stated. A real analysis is needed.

comments.author: whershberger
comments.body:
There are two standing issues with these patches:

- get_global_pool_hard_max_size parses /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly, resulting in the default value being used unconditionally
- The default value returned by get_global_pool_hard_max_size is UINT_MAX; a better/conservative choice would be the kernel's default max_map_count (65530)

We've submitted upstream patches to resolve both of these issues; neither have been merged to qemu's master yet.

https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/qemu-devel/2026-10/msg04337.html
